messages.author: caedf03f93a485b2
messages.subject: 64-bit installation error in sfit
parts:
Dear list,

I just successfully installed aroma.affymetrix onto a 64-bit Solaris
10 system, and thought I would post what may be a bug in the
installation of "sfit" (and more importantly, the solution).

I have searched the archives, and Henrik mentioned that sfit shouldn't
install by default? This seems not to be the case. sfit is a
dependency of GLAM, and thus is required.

Because i'm using R-64bit, which was built from source, most new
packages that I install, that also require compilation manage to
retrieve the appropriate compiler/linker flags from an unkown (by me)
location. I think there's a config.site style of file somewhere that
contains the appropriate CC, CFLAGS, LDFLAGS etc variables that I set
when installing R. The most important flags (for compiling in 64-bit)
seem to be -m64 and -mcpu=v9

Using the suggested method of installing aroma.affymetrix (see below)
I was able to install all required packages except for sfit (and
GLAM), and I tracked the error down to the Makefile within the sfit
package, which does not realise that i'm trying to compile in 64bit,
ie doesn't find the appropriate installation options that nearly all
other packages that require compilation are able to find.


I installed using the recommended:

source("http://www.braju.com/R/hbLite.R")
hbInstall("aroma.affymetrix")


The error was:
# * Installing to library '/usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/
library'
# * Installing *source* package 'sfit' ...
# ** libs
# ** arch -
# gcc -Wall -O3 -I/usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/include -I/
usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/include -I/usr/local/include -
fPIC -g -O -m64 -mcpu=v9 -c cfit.c -o cfit.o
# gcc -Wall -O3 -I/usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/include -I/
usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/include -I/usr/local/include -
fPIC -g -O -m64 -mcpu=v9 -c spa.c -o spa.o
# gcc -O3 cli.c cfit.o spa.o -o cfit -lm
# ld: fatal: file cfit.o: wrong ELF class: ELFCLASS64
# ld: fatal: File processing errors. No output written to cfit
# collect2: ld returned 1 exit status
# make: *** [cfit] Error 1
# ERROR: compilation failed for package 'sfit'
# ** Removing '/usr/local/lib/R-2.6.0-64bit/lib/R/library/sfit'

This error is because the compilation command "gcc -O3 cli.c cfit.o
spa.o -o cfit -lm" should be "gcc -O3 -m64 -mcpu=v9 cli.c cfit.o
spa.o -o cfit -lm"

The solution was (see two lines with ">>>"):
cat /tmp/RtmpZy5ZIi/downloaded_packages/sfit/src/Makefile
# INCLUDES = ${HOME}/include
# LIBS = ${HOME}/lib
>>> # CC = gcc -Wall -O3 -m64 -mcpu=v9
#
# all: cfit
# cp cfit dummy.so
# mv cfit ../inst/bin/
#
# cfit: cfit.o spa.o cli.c spa.h
>>> # $(CC) cli.c cfit.o spa.o -o cfit -lm
#
# test: cfit dye2.dat
# cfit 5 dye2.dat -a .01 -d 1 --outM stdout -q 10 -Q 90
#
# clean:
# rm -f ../inst/bin/cfit
# rm -f dummy.so
# rm -f *.o
#
#
######################################################################
# # HISTORY:
# # 2006-05-20
# # o Added a clean rule.
# # o Added a rule to move the build binary to ../inst/bin/ when
done.
# # 2006-05-16
# # o Removed -liberty from gcc in cfit target. /HB
#
######################################################################

Correct output is:
$ make
# gcc -Wall -O3 -m64 -mcpu=v9 -c -o cfit.o cfit.c
# gcc -Wall -O3 -m64 -mcpu=v9 -c -o spa.o spa.c
# gcc -Wall -O3 -m64 -mcpu=v9 cli.c cfit.o spa.o -o cfit -lm
# cli.c: In function `main':
# cli.c:88: warning: 'f' might be used uninitialized in this
function
# cp cfit dummy.so
# mv cfit ../inst/bin/

Now that this can compile, i rebuilt the R package, and then installed
it as follows:
$ make clean
$ cd /tmp/RtmpZy5ZIi/downloaded_packages
$ R CMD build sfit
$ R CMD INSTALL sfit_0.1.5.tar.gz

Admittedly, I don't fully understand the magic that configure scripts
perform, and how installing R packages seems to find the correct
compiler/linker flags; however, it's clear the fairly simple Makefile
for sfit could benefit from finding these flags?

I hope this post helps users, and perhaps someone can let me know
where R finds its flags from under normal operation?

cheers,
Mark

** R

I was at WEHI, Melbourne, they also had 64-bit machines. When you

flag etc) is specific to Sun 64-bit systems, or not.

>

Your observation is correct, and does not surprise me, although I
cannot reproduce it. The reason is that 'sfit' is quite special. So,
the C code for 'sfit' were written by a P. Wirapati (WEHI at the time)
who did not use R but compiled code to executable. So, he had a set
of command line tools that took certain arguments and read data from
file and wrote results back to file. He had a Makefile for this.
What I've done, is basically to create R wrappers that write data to
temp file, calls his executables, and reads data back. It is
basically lack of time (for 2+ yrs) that prevents me from writing R
.Call() wrappers to his C functions. Anyone, help is always
appreciated ;)

More comments below.

>

So, what you observe below is that the R installer first search for
all native code (here *.c files) and uses *its* settings/options to
compile those. This is why 'cfit.c' and 'spa.c' are compiles with the
' -m64 -mcpu=v9' flags that are specific to your system. Then, R
looks for a Makefile and if it exists, it is called. Since cfit.o and
spa.o already exists (built by R), 'make' goes to the rule:

which is called. Now, since this is hardwired in the package, you get
the above error.

>
> The solution was (see two lines with ">>>"):
> cat /tmp/RtmpZy5ZIi/downloaded_packages/sfit/src/Makefile
> # INCLUDES = ${HOME}/include
> # LIBS = ${HOME}/lib
> >>> # CC = gcc -Wall -O3 -m64 -mcpu=v9

Ok, this is where I am also a bit lost. We basically want to insert
those R specific compiler options into the Makescript, but this should
be dynamic and not static. Your solution (below) works if edited
manually. So, something like:

CC = gcc -Wall -O3 ${RCCFLAGSHERE}

but I don't know the details. Anyone, do you know if this is possible
and then where to grab the R compiler flags?

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] 64-bit installation error in sfit
parts:
Hi again,

so I looked at the R documentation a little bit more and my best guess
is that variables CC and/or CFLAGS contain the compiler specific
flags. Mark, could you please try to rebuild 'sfit' with the
following Makefile and the try to reinstall:
INCLUDES = ${HOME}/include
LIBS = ${HOME}/lib

PKG_CFLAGS = -Wall -O3

all: cfit
cp cfit dummy.so
mv cfit ../inst/bin/
cfit: cfit.o spa.o cli.c spa.h

$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(PKG_CFLAGS) cli.c cfit.o spa.o -o cfit -lm

test: cfit dye2.dat
cfit 5 dye2.dat -a .01 -d 1 --outM stdout -q 10 -Q 90

clean:
rm -f ../inst/bin/cfit
rm -f dummy.so
rm -f *.o

Could you please cut'n'paste the output where the compile is process
(as last time)? I've tried the above script on both WinXP and Linux
at there it works, but again, neither uses -m64 etc. If it works on
your system as well, I'll commit a fix.

Henrik
